The operation: start with reachable tasks, add difficulty or constraints gradually, and block unsafe updates. For RAIL: Reachability-Aided Imitation Learning for Safety, the added step is: reachability constraints keep imitation safe. In plain terms, the paper changes where reward comes from, what action space is searched, or how experience is reused.

Why the math helps: Curriculum and safety constraints keep learning from collapsing before the policy has basic competence. The important principle is credit assignment: connect the eventual outcome back to the earlier action choices that caused it.
RAIL: Reachability-Aided Imitation Learn.work: A legged robot learns to walk from 2000 expert trajectories. Without reachability constraints, imitation learning crashes during exploration (~20% of rollouts fail within 5 steps, costing $40k per hardware fall). Constraining actions to reachable states (verified via forward model), crash rate drops to 0.5%, reducing expected hardware repair cost from $8k to $20 per training run — a 400× safety gain.

Uncertainty-Aware Input-Constrained Cont.work: A robot arm learning to reach targets in a partially observable workspace has ±0.2 m position uncertainty. Naive RL violates safety (knocking over objects) on 18% of 500 trial rollouts. Control Barrier Functions that account for uncertainty tighten the action set, reducing safety violations to 0.4% — a 45× drop — while sacrificing only 3% of baseline task speed.
